headline: Broad demand growth drives sharply higher margins, profit
summary_short: Amkor's Q2 FY2026 revenue rose to $1,898M (+12.7% q/q, +25.6% y/y) on growth across every end market, while gross margin expanded to 16.8% from 12.0% a year ago on higher factory utilization, pushing net income to $174M and diluted EPS to $0.70.
summary_long: Revenue rose 12.7% q/q and 25.6% y/y to $1,898M on growth across every end market: communications +32%, automotive/industrial +35% (premium smartphones, ADAS, industrial), and computing +23% on datacenter strength. Gross margin expanded to 16.8% from 12.0% y/y on higher factory utilization tied to the sales increase; operating margin rose to 10.5% from 6.1% on that margin gain plus a gain on disposal of fixed assets, partly offset by comparison against a 2025 Nanium bankruptcy-proceeds receipt that had boosted the year-ago quarter. Net income more than tripled y/y to $174M; diluted EPS reached $0.70 versus $0.22. Cash plus short-term investments rose to $2.51B after May's $1.15B convertible-notes issuance. FY2026 capex guidance stands at $2.5-3.0B, up on Arizona Facility construction.

drivers.explanation: Broad-based demand growth across every end market, combined with higher factory utilization on a largely fixed cost base, drove margins and profitability sharply higher against a weak year-ago quarter.
Growth across all end markets: communications +32%, automotive/industrial +35% on premium-tier smartphone content and ADAS/industrial demand, and computing +23% on datacenter strength.
Higher factory utilization driven by the increase in net sales, given Amkor's high proportion of fixed manufacturing costs.
Reflects the gross-margin gain plus a gain on disposal of fixed assets, partly offset by comparison against a 2025 Nanium Insolvency Receipt that had boosted the year-ago quarter's operating income.
Not separately explained in the release beyond the operating income drivers above.
